answers.charter-meetings: The committee must meet **at least four times per year** [1]. It must also meet at least annually with the audit committee [1], including a joint meeting at least annually to review major non-financial compliance matters [2].
answers.charter-min-directors: Under the charter, the ethics and compliance committee must have **no fewer than three non-employee directors**, each meeting the New York Stock Exchange standards for director independence [1].
answers.charter-term-length: Committee members are appointed by the board for **one-year terms**, on the recommendation of the directors and corporate governance committee. They serve such terms as the board may determine, or until their earlier removal, resignation, or death [1].
answers.charter-financial-oversight: The **audit committee** has sole oversight over financial compliance, which covers accounting, auditing, financial reporting, and related investor disclosures. The ethics and compliance committee has primary oversight of all other areas ("non-financial compliance"), and the two committees meet jointly at least annually to review major non-financial compliance matters [1].
answers.charter-section-name: According to the Composition and Term section, **the chair shall be designated by the board** [1].
answers.redbook-report-concern: Under the Red Book, anyone, whether working for Lilly or not, can submit concerns about possible violations of laws and regulations, the Red Book, or company policies or procedures at https://speakup.lilly.com [1]. Under the Supplier Code of Business Conduct, known or suspected violations can be reported to Lilly sponsors or the Lilly Ethics & Compliance Hotline at www.lillyethics.ethicspoint.com or 1-800-815-2481 [2][3].
answers.redbook-values: Lilly's values are **Integrity, Excellence, and Respect for People** [1][3]. Lilly expects its suppliers and employees to conduct Lilly business consistent with these values and its high standards of corporate conduct [1].
answers.redbook-last-step: The last step is **Step 5: Reflect and Learn**. It asks: What went well? What could be improved? Are there lessons to share with your team? [2]
answers.redbook-ai-bias: According to the Red Book, Lilly **strives to mitigate any inherent bias or discrimination in data, information, or algorithms** [1]. This is part of its commitment to the responsible use of AI. That commitment also includes protecting against unintended applications, unintended access, and harm, employing technology that produces valid and reliable outputs, and promoting transparency [1].
answers.redbook-investigations: Yes. Investigation details, including discipline, are treated as confidential [1].
answers.supplier-excluded-employee: A supplier must report to Lilly **within five (5) calendar days** if one of its employees is excluded or restricted in any way from doing business with any government [1][2].
answers.supplier-death-report: Under the Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct, any known or suspected death or suspect product must be reported **immediately (within 24 hours of receipt)** [1][2]. In the US, the report goes to The Lilly Answers Center (TLAC) at 1.800.LillyRx (1.800.545.5979), or through an alternative reporting method determined by the Lilly component [1][2].
answers.supplier-hotline-number: The Lilly Ethics & Compliance Hotline phone number is **1-800-815-2481**. It can also be reached online at www.lillyethics.ethicspoint.com.
answers.supplier-cooperative-learning: Cooperative learning programs are mentioned only as an example of an exception to the child labor rule. The Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct states: "We do not use child labor (except as consistent with applicable law, such as cooperative learning programs)" [1][2].
answers.supplier-impaired: No. The Lilly Supplier Code of Business Conduct states, "we ensure that we are not impaired with drugs or alcohol while at work so that we can be fully engaged and help make life better for people around the world" [1][3]. This falls under the commitment to "bring our full selves to work each day."
answers.charter-statutes-reworded: The **ethics and compliance committee** does this. Its charter says it "shall review, identify, and when appropriate bring to the attention of the board of directors legal and regulatory trends and issues" that "may have an impact on the business operations, financial performance or reputation of the company."
answers.charter-statutes-typo: The **ethics and compliance committee** is responsible. Under its charter, the committee "shall review, identify, and when appropriate bring to the attention of the board of directors legal and regulatory trends and issues" that may affect the company's business operations, financial performance, or reputation.
answers.supplier-adverse-event: Report any adverse event or product complaint **within one business day**, and any known or suspected death or suspect product **immediately (within 24 hours of receipt)**. Outside the US, select your location from the globe link in the upper right corner of Lilly.com, then click "Contact" or "Contact Us" in the top menu bar to access the appropriate local reporting method.
answers.retaliation: No, Lilly does not tolerate retaliation for reporting inappropriate conduct, preventing unlawful practices, or participating in an investigation, and it takes appropriate measures to prevent retaliation against people who make reports [1][2]. Employees can share concerns openly and honestly, even anonymously, knowing that Lilly will not tolerate acts of retaliation [3]. Retaliation is also listed among the inappropriate conduct that Lilly does not tolerate [4].
answers.supplier-purchasing: Under excerpt [2], purchasing goods or services requires **authorization from procurement, assessment by third party risk management, and appropriate supporting contractual documentation**. Excerpt [1], which appears to be a different version of the same section, lists only **authorization from procurement and appropriate supporting documentation**. Both versions also require **appropriate authority and the required Lilly approvals** before acquiring or committing Lilly resources or disbursing Lilly funds.
answers.supplier-gifts-on-behalf: No, not without prior written approval. Lilly does "not allow our suppliers to offer gifts or donations on Lilly's behalf without prior written approval" [1][2].
answers.supplier-current-version: The most recent version in the provided excerpts is **V15.0 (©2025)**, according to excerpt [2]. An earlier version, 13.0 (©2021), also appears in excerpt [1]. The excerpts do not say which version is designated as current.
answers.vacation-days: This is not covered in the provided policy documents.
